chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
that he forbade slandering one who was upon other than Islam, except that you had come to know that from him.

key_terms.اطَّلَعْتَ: You came to know / gained knowledge
key_terms.قَذْف: Slander or attributing a specific fault (often chastity-related) to someone

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia ruling on slandering non-Muslims?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'qadhf' (slander) extending to non-Muslims, contingent upon the accuser's personal knowledge of the fault. It reflects the Shia scholarly view that general slander is prohibited regardless of the target's faith, provided the accuser has direct evidence ('ittila'') of the specific attribute being attributed. This ruling underscores the importance of precision in testimony and avoids the injustice of baseless accusations against the 'Ahl al-Kitab' or other non-Muslims.
